items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: And in the interim, I had Johnny Hodges come in and do a couple of our record dates

ctx.x: No, I didn't. I was playing tenor with Isham, and sometimes baritone, and I was doing mostly clarinet soloing. And then when we started the band, I was going to play clarinet exclusively, and not mess with the saxophone section at all. And I did, for several years. I had a temperamental alto player, it doesn't matter who it was, who gave us a lot of problems, and particularly on one record date or another. And I became a little annoyed and borrowed an alto from one of the other guys, and played a couple of things…

And we decided that maybe that would be the best move. And I played some of those things. And in the interim, I had Johnny Hodges come in and do a couple of our record dates, and Ben Webster and a lot of other people, because Ellington's band was -- it was one of those periods with Duke's band where the boys were getting nervous in the band. They were complaining that Duke was taking their backgrounds and making tunes out of them, and a lot of internal strife for that moment. And so they were all -- I would hear…
